The inbound email flow is in `SiftOrder/src/main/java/com/siftit/domain/emailReceiving/InvoiceEmailService.java`. I haven't run anything, so this comes from reading the code only.

Most failures are saved in the `emailReceivingRecord` table, in the `errors` column (`EmailReceivingRecord.java:27`). Admins can retrieve them with `getErrors()` (`InvoiceEmailService.java:243`). The raw email stays in S3 under the key stored on the record.

| # | Reason | Where it's recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The recipient address couldn't be resolved, for example a bad `to`, `cc` or `bcc` header. | The error is added at `InvoiceRecipientResolver.java:76` and saved in `errors`. |
| 2 | No address looks like `<id>@invoices…`. | The error is added at `:163` and saved in `errors`. The S3 key is `noLocalPart/<file>` (`:162`). |
| 3 | The local part isn't a known restaurant ID, or it isn't numeric. The lookup swallows its exceptions (`:200-202`). | The error is added at `:160` and saved in `errors`. The S3 key is `unknown/<localPart>/…` (`:159`). |
| 4 | The restaurant is inactive. | The error "Restaurant was not marked active" is added at `:125` and saved in `errors`. The attachment is skipped. |
| 5 | The attachment isn't an accepted type. Only JPEG, PNG, BMP, PDF, JPG and GIF count as images (`:52`), and TXT and CSV count as text (`:53`). A PDF with a wrong or missing extension fails here. | The error is added at `:141` and saved in `errors`. |
| 6 | The attachment is a TXT or CSV and the sender's domain has no supplier mapping. Only `rnc.sysco.com` is mapped (`:69`). | The error is added at `:138` and saved in `errors`. |
| 7 | Saving the attachment threw an exception, from `saveNewGroupingForInvoice` or `addInvoiceAttachment`. | The error is added at `:144` and saved in `errors`. |
| 8 | The MIME message couldn't be parsed at all (`FallbackMimeParser.java:40,50`). | It's logged via `orderlyLogger` at `:182`, tagged `InvoiceEmail`. No record is saved. The S3 file is moved to `unparsable/…` (`:183`). |
| 9 | Any other exception in `handleEmail`, or in saving the record or moving the S3 file. | It's logged via `orderlyLogger` at `:168` and `:185`. No record is saved. The email stays under `invoices/`, so the next run retries it. |
| 10 | The job never ran. `handleUnparsedEmails` returns immediately in dev (`:91`). | Nothing is recorded. |

Two things to know when debugging:
- The attachment-level errors (#4 to #7) only apply when a restaurant was found (`:119`). Otherwise only the restaurant-level error appears.
- An email with no attachments at all produces a record with empty `allAttachments` and no error, so it looks like nothing happened.
